hints.title: Permutational Sum Count Obstacle
hints.text: Different sequences of numbers that add up to target are counted as distinct combinations. How can stepping through each possible ending value build the total permutations for each intermediate target?

hints.title: Ordered Sum Transition Invariant
hints.text: The number of ordered sequences summing to target t is the sum of combinations for t - num across all num in nums where num <= t.

hints.title: 1D Array Bottom-Up Target Progression Procedure
hints.text: Create an array of size target + 1 initialized to zeros, with base case entry 0 set to 1. Loop through every intermediate value t from 1 to target. Inside, iterate through each number in nums: if t >= num, add entry t - num to entry t. Return entry target.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Computes ordered combination counts for each target value up to T.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Recursive branching without state tabulation takes O(N^T) exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Array of size T + 1 uses minimal memory to store all sub-target combinations.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizing that outer loop over target and inner loop over numbers counts ordered permutations rather than unordered combinations.
